:::{#thm-arithmetic-code-length}
#### The expected length of an arithmetic code

Let $X$ be a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv)
that takes a finite number of values, each with positive [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability),
and let $\entropyf{X}$ be its [entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy)
with base-2 [logarithms](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm).
Then the [arithmetic code](#def-arithmetic-code) for $n$ independent copies of $X$
has [expected length](source-coding.qmd#def-expected-length)

$$\expcodelen < n \entropyf{X} + 2,$$

which is fewer than $\entropyf{X} + 2/n$ binary digits per copy.

:::

::: {.proof}

By @lem-arithmetic-interval,
the final interval of a message $x = (x_1, \ldots, x_n)$ has width $w = \pf{x_1} \cdots \pf{x_n}$.
So the [codeword length](source-coding.qmd#def-code) satisfies

$$\codelenf{x} = \ceil{-\log_2 w} + 1 < -\log_2 w + 2 = \sumto{i}{n} \paren{-\log_2 \pf{x_i}} + 2.$$

Taking expectations,
and using that each copy $X_i$ has the [expectation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-expectation) $\E{-\log_2 \pf{X_i}} = \entropyf{X}$,
gives $\expcodelen < n \entropyf{X} + 2$.
Dividing by $n$ gives the bound per copy.

:::
